proposed_english: the wretched ones / the random ones
rationale: Likely from Greek τύχη / τυχαῖος / τυχόντες — 'the random, the casual, the worldly-fated.' Refers to the wicked who have laid up treasure under the Devil. Confidence moderate; awaits parallels.
Lycopolitan variant numeral 'ten' (= Sah. ⲙⲏⲧ). Distinguished from ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥⲉ '12' and ⲙⲏⲧ '10'. Recognizable by the prosthetic ⲛ̄ and final ⲏ.
Lycopolitan 3sgm habitual ϣⲁϩ- + ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'recompense, requite' (Sah. ⲧⲟⲩⲉⲓⲟ / ⲧⲱⲱⲃⲉ). The verb governs ⲛⲉⲩ 'to them' + ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ 'with providence-service' — divine reciprocity-formula.

Lycopolitan conjunctive verb of placing/setting/finding + 3pl object. Etymology unclear; possibly from ϩⲉ 'find' or ϩⲱⲧⲉ 'set, place'. Functions here as 'and (He) renders them as inheritors'. Confidence moderate.

proposed_english: escape, lest / escape, so as not to
rationale: Compound construction ⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'escape' (in glossary) + ⲁⲧⲉ negative-purpose conjunctive 'lest'. The catechumen escapes precisely to prevent his wealth from going by the three ways to Gehenna.

Manichaean technical-cosmological term for the ten paths drawn from the Zone (zodiacal girdle). Subdivided into 4 (to light/life), and 6 (gehenna and transmutation paths) — though the body-text gives 4 + 8 = 12, with 'ten' as the canonical/headline count.

Tentative parsing: ⲁⲡⲡⲉ = 'to the height' (Lyc. with double article ⲡ-ⲡⲉ for ⲡⲧⲡⲉ 'heaven') + ⲭⲛ̄ (Lyc. ϫⲓⲛ) 'from'. Alternative: ⲁⲡⲡⲉⲭⲛ̄ as single unidentified locus-noun. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.
